transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We've got the weekend shift coming up on Line 6 with 900 cartons to package, and we need to go through the pre-run review before I can authorize the run. As you know, we're planning to use the new robotic palletizer — it's already validated for barcode scanning and sorting into the family groups, so we don't need a separate controls review on that. What I need from you two are your findings: maintenance lead, what's your assessment of the robotic palletizer? And quality engineer, what's your review? I need both before I can sign off.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a serious issue. During my commissioning check of the robotic palletizer, I found that the safety interlock is not holding reliably. Maintenance policy prohibits using the robot for this weekend's run because of that. The good news is we can prepare the manual palletizing station as a fallback in exactly 45 minutes with two trained operators. I should also note that I haven't entered the finding in the maintenance work order yet because the commissioning packet is still awaiting my supervisor's signature, but the safety concern is real and I can't recommend we run the robot this weekend.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important detail from the customer's pilot-packaging instruction that I confirmed. All 900 cartons must receive a barcode scan and be palletized into exactly three family groups: 300 cartons of Family X, 280 cartons of Family Y, and 320 cartons of Family Z. I haven't uploaded the instruction to the quality system yet because the customer service team is still linking the purchase-order revision, but this is a confirmed customer requirement for this run.
transcript.speaker: A3
